Automationv1DraftNot implemented

Slice: Collect Hold

Step 6 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · after Holds To Collect · before My Holds — hold collected · Automation

Intent

When a holder checks out the tool they hold, record that their hold was collected, so the hold ends as a Holds fact and the views about holds hear it from their own context. Checking out records only Tool Checked Out; Hold Collected is recorded separately, by this slice. The system does this itself; no person collects a hold.

What follows a collection is decided by the slices that read Hold Collected: the hold leaves My Holds, Holds To Fulfill's queue, Pickup Notices To Send and Pickups To Expire, and a failed pickup email for it leaves Undelivered Notices.

Trigger & Actor

  • Pattern: automation. The Hold Collector, a system processor, watches the Holds To Collect list (slices/holds-to-collect.md). Only the Hold Collector issues Collect Hold; it is not exposed to neighbors or the shed manager.
  • Triggering condition: a hold is on the list: its holder has an open loan on its tool.
  • When it acts: the list changes only when a checkout lands, so the collector acts whenever the list changes, on each item that appears.
  • What it does: it issues Collect Hold for the item's hold and loan. If the command is refused or is a repeat, nothing is recorded and the processor moves on.

Command / Input

Command: Collect Hold

HoldId and LoanId are UUIDs.

FieldTypeRequiredRules / Validation
holdIdHoldIdyesThe hold collected. Must be a hold that has been placed (INV-COL-5) and is still live (INV-COL-2).
loanIdLoanIdyesThe loan that collected it, from the list item: the holder's open loan on the hold's tool (INV-COL-3).

Trigger

Triggered by: processor Hold Collector, also in this slice, reading Holds To Collect.

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Hold Collected → context Holds Read by: Holds To Collect (the hold leaves the list), My Holds (the hold drops off), Holds To Fulfill (the hold leaves the queue), Pickup Notices To Send and Pickups To Expire (the set-aside ends), Undelivered Notices (a pickup-notice entry drops off).

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
holdIdHoldIdyesFrom the command.
toolIdToolIdyesSet by the system: the tool on the hold's Hold Placed.
neighborIdNeighborIdyesSet by the system: the holder on the hold's Hold Placed.
loanIdLoanIdyesFrom the command: the loan that collected the hold.
collectedAtInstantyesSet by the system: the UTC moment the event is recorded.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Hold Collected takes the hold off Holds To Collect, My Holds, Holds To Fulfill, Pickup Notices To Send, Pickups To Expire and Undelivered Notices, each specified in its own doc and eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-COL-1: Only the Hold Collector collects holds, and only from Holds To Collect.
  • INV-COL-2: A hold is collected only while it is live: placed, and not cancelled, expired or already collected.
    • A hold cancelled in the moment between the checkout and the collector acting is refused hold-ended, and stays ended.
  • INV-COL-3: The loan named must be the holder's open loan on the hold's tool.
    • The collector takes it from the list item; a different loan is a faulty caller.
  • INV-COL-4: Collecting a hold already collected succeeds and records nothing.
  • INV-COL-5: The hold must exist.
  • INV-COL-6: Collect Hold records only Hold Collected.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ben's hold H1 is live on the cordless drill (T1), and Tool Checked Out was recorded for T1 and Ben as loan L5.

  • Happy path (INV-COL-1, INV-COL-3, INV-COL-6)
    • Given: H1 is on Holds To Collect with loan L5
    • When: the Hold Collector issues Collect Hold for H1 and L5
    • Then: Hold Collected is recorded for H1: tool T1, holder Ben, loan L5, and the moment. Nothing else is recorded.
  • Front hold collected before the set-aside (INV-COL-2)
    • Given: H1 was never fulfilled; Ben took T1 from the front of the queue
    • When: the Hold Collector issues Collect Hold for H1 and L5
    • Then: Hold Collected is recorded for H1.
  • Collected twice (INV-COL-4)
    • Given: Hold Collected has been recorded for H1
    • When: the Hold Collector issues Collect Hold for H1 and L5 again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Cancelled before the collector acts (INV-COL-2)
    • Given: Hold Cancelled was recorded for H1 after the checkout
    • When: the Hold Collector issues Collect Hold for H1 and L5
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.
  • Wrong loan (INV-COL-3)
    • Given: H1 is on the list with loan L5
    • When: Collect Hold arrives for H1 and L9
    • Then: refused with loan-mismatch. No event is recorded.
  • Unknown hold (INV-COL-5)
    • Given: no hold has ID H9
    • When: Collect Hold arrives for H9
    • Then: refused with hold-not-found. No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

A refusal records nothing. No person sees these reasons; they are logged with the hold ID. The name is the contract; the sentence is the log text.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. hold-not-found (INV-COL-5).
  2. If Hold Collected is already recorded for the hold, the command succeeds and records nothing (INV-COL-4).
  3. hold-ended (INV-COL-2).
  4. loan-mismatch (INV-COL-3).
ReasonSentenceRule
hold-not-foundThere is no such hold.INV-COL-5
hold-endedThis hold has already ended.INV-COL-2
loan-mismatchThis loan did not collect this hold.INV-COL-3

hold-not-found and hold-ended mean the same conditions as in Cancel Hold. A missing or malformed hold ID or loan ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: a collection is identified by its hold. A repeat after Hold Collected succeeds and records nothing. The collector may read the same item twice before Hold Collected lands; the second attempt is the repeat above.

Requests at the same moment: Collect Hold is decided against the hold's events as already recorded, one at a time per hold, so at most one Hold Collected is recorded for a hold.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: internal; only the Hold Collector issues it (INV-COL-1).
  • PII & compliance: ids and a time only.
  • Performance / SLA: a hold is collected shortly after its checkout lands (seconds, not minutes); until then the hold views still show it, as the doc of each says.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold and the slices that repeat it), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Collected (this slice): holdId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId.
    • These keys match slices/place-hold.md, slices/cancel-hold.md and slices/check-out-tool.md.
  • Read model this slice's processor reads: Holds To Collect (slices/holds-to-collect.md).
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Holds To Collect, My Holds, Holds To Fulfill, Pickup Notices To Send, Pickups To Expire and Undelivered Notices.

Open Questions

None.

Slice: Cancel Hold

Step 9 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · after Undelivered Notices — hold collected · before My Holds — hold cancelled · State Change

Intent

Let a neighbor give up a hold they no longer want, from My Holds, so the tool goes to the next neighbor in the queue instead of waiting on them. A hold can be cancelled while it is waiting or while the tool is set aside for the holder, and a suspended neighbor can cancel too.

What follows a cancellation is decided by the views and slices that read Hold Cancelled:

  • Every hold behind the cancelled one on that tool moves up one place (My Holds, Holds To Fulfill).
  • Cancelling a hold that is ready for pickup ends the set-aside. The tool passes to the next hold, or becomes available if none is waiting (Holds To Fulfill, Tool Catalog), the same as when a set-aside expires.
  • A cancelled hold gives up its place for good. The neighbor may place a new hold on the same tool, which joins the back of the queue (Place Hold, INV-HOLD-7: only a live hold counts).

Trigger & Actor

The holder, from the My Holds screen, on one of their own holds that hasn't ended. The shed manager doesn't cancel holds. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID.

Command / Input

Command: Cancel Hold

A HoldId or NeighborId is a UUID.

FieldTypeRequiredRules / Validation
holdIdHoldIdyesThe hold to cancel. Must be a hold that has been placed (INV-CNH-7).
neighborIdNeighborIdyesThe neighbor cancelling, who must be the one making the request (requester-mismatch) and the hold's holder (not-your-hold) (INV-CNH-1).

Trigger

Triggered by: screen My Holds @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Hold Cancelled → context Holds Read by: My Holds and Tool Catalog (their continuations right after this slice), My Loans (whether a hold is still waiting on a borrowed tool), Holds To Fulfill and Pickups To Expire (the hold's queue and set-aside), Pickup Notices To Send (no pickup email for a cancelled set-aside), and Undelivered Notices (a failed pickup email's entry drops off).

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
holdIdHoldIdyesFrom the command. The tool and holder are those on the hold's Hold Placed.
cancelledAtInstantyesThe UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.

The event doesn't say whether the hold was waiting or set aside. Readers already know from Hold Placed and Hold Fulfilled.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Hold Cancelled ends the hold in My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans and the hold to-do lists, each specified in its own doc. All are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-CNH-1: A neighbor can cancel only their own hold, and does it themselves.
    • The command names the acting neighbor in neighborId. The request must come from that neighbor (requester-mismatch), and the hold must be theirs (not-your-hold). The shed manager does not cancel holds. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID.
    • A caller with no sign-in is refused with not-signed-in, before anything else is checked.
  • INV-CNH-2: A hold can be cancelled while it is waiting or while the tool is set aside for the holder.
    • A suspended neighbor may cancel their own hold. Cancelling only gives up their own claim.
    • A set-aside whose collect-by date has passed, but whose Hold Expired hasn't been recorded yet, hasn't ended, so it can still be cancelled. Either way the tool passes on.
  • INV-CNH-3: A hold that has ended in any way other than being cancelled can't be cancelled.
    • A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, the holder checks the tool out, the tool is retired or recorded lost, or the holder closes their account.
    • A hold the holder has already cancelled is covered by INV-CNH-8.
  • INV-CNH-7: The hold must exist.
  • INV-CNH-8: Cancelling a hold that is already cancelled succeeds and records nothing new.
    • So a double submit, or a retry after a lost response, never fails and never records a second Hold Cancelled.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ben and Cara are active neighbors, and Ben's hold H1 on the cordless drill was placed before Cara's hold H2.

  • Cancel a waiting hold (INV-CNH-2)
    • Given: the drill is checked out by Ana, and H1 and H2 are waiting
    • When: Ben cancels H1 from My Holds
    • Then: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1.
  • Cancel a hold that is ready for pickup (INV-CNH-2)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben under H1, with a collect-by date of 17 October, and H2 is waiting
    • When: Ben cancels H1 on 15 October
    • Then: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1.
  • Cancel a lapsed set-aside before its expiry is recorded (INV-CNH-2)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben under H1, to collect by 17 October. It is 18 October and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded for H1.
    • When: Ben cancels H1
    • Then: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1, and no Hold Expired follows for it.
  • Suspended neighbor cancels a hold (INV-CNH-2)
    • Given: Ben is suspended, and H1 is waiting
    • When: Ben cancels H1
    • Then: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-CNH-8)
    • Given: Hold Cancelled has been recorded for H1
    • When: the same request to cancel H1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • A request that doesn't come from the neighbor it names (INV-CNH-1)
    • Given: H1 is Ben's waiting hold
    • When: a request to cancel H1, naming Ben, comes from someone other than Ben
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only cancel holds for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • Someone else's hold (INV-CNH-1)
    • Given: H1 is Ben's waiting hold
    • When: Cara, naming herself, tries to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with not-your-hold: "You can only cancel your own holds." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown hold (INV-CNH-7)
    • Given: no hold H9 has been placed
    • When: a request to cancel H9 arrives
    • Then: refused with hold-not-found: "There is no such hold." No event is recorded.
  • Hold already expired (INV-CNH-3)
    • Given: Hold Expired has been recorded for H1
    • When: Ben tries to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended: "This hold has already ended." No event is recorded.
  • Hold ended by the holder's checkout (INV-CNH-3)
    • Given: Ben checked out the drill as H1's holder, which ended H1
    • When: Ben tries to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.
  • Hold ended by retirement (INV-CNH-3)
    • Given: the drill was retired while H1 was waiting
    • When: Ben tries to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.
  • Hold ended because the tool was recorded lost (INV-CNH-3)
    • Given: Tool Lost was recorded for Ana's loan of the drill while H1 was waiting
    • When: Ben tries to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.
  • Hold ended by closing the account (INV-CNH-3)
    • Given: Ben closed his account while H1 was waiting
    • When: a request to cancel H1 for Ben arrives
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded.
  • No sign-in (INV-CNH-1)
    • Given: a caller with no sign-in
    • When: they ask to cancel H1
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the neighbor on the My Holds screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in, then requester-mismatch (INV-CNH-1).
  2. hold-not-found (INV-CNH-7).
  3. not-your-hold (INV-CNH-1).
  4. If Hold Cancelled is already recorded for the hold, the request succeeds and records nothing (INV-CNH-8).
  5. hold-ended (INV-CNH-3).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-CNH-1
requester-mismatchYou can only cancel holds for yourself.INV-CNH-1
hold-not-foundThere is no such hold.INV-CNH-7
not-your-holdYou can only cancel your own holds.INV-CNH-1
hold-endedThis hold has already ended.INV-CNH-3

hold-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. hold-not-found is worded the same wherever a hold is looked up.

Idempotency: cancelling is safe to repeat (INV-CNH-8). A repeat records nothing, whatever has happened since.

Requests at the same moment: each cancellation is decided against the hold's events as already recorded, one at a time per hold. If the holder cancels just as the hold ends another way (the fulfiller sets the tool aside, the expirer expires it, or the tool is retired), whichever is recorded first stands. A cancel decided after an expiry, retirement or closure is refused with hold-ended. A cancel decided after Hold Fulfilled cancels the set-aside.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. Cancelling sends no email.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the holder may cancel their own hold (INV-CNH-1). Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the acting neighbor's ID.
  • PII & compliance: Hold Cancelled holds only the hold's ID and a time. No name or email.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Cancelled (this slice): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): toolId, neighborId (the holder's own checkout ends their hold on that tool).
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): toolId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match slices/place-hold.md, check-out-tool.md and tool-catalog.md. Hold Cancelled adds cancelledAt; readers that need only {holdId} are unaffected.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans, Holds To Fulfill, Pickups To Expire, Pickup Notices To Send and Undelivered Notices. Place Hold accepts a new hold from the same neighbor on the same tool once this one is cancelled.

Open Questions

  • Dependencies: Tool Lost is matched by its own toolId, not through Tool Checked Out.loanId (conformance 2026-11-01, finding 5) — v2: Dependencies reworded; behaviour unchanged (2026-11-01)

Automationv2DraftDelta pending

Slice: Fulfill Hold

Step 15 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · after Holds To Fulfill · before Tool Catalog — hold fulfilled · Automation

Intent

When a tool is back in the shed with holds waiting, set it aside for the neighbor at the front of the queue, so the tool goes to holders in the order they asked. The system does this itself; no person decides it. Returning a tool records only Tool Returned; Hold Fulfilled is recorded separately, by this slice.

What follows a fulfilment is decided by the slices that read Hold Fulfilled: the holder is emailed that the tool is ready (Send Pickup Notice, which doesn't hold up the fulfilment), My Holds shows it ready for pickup with its collect-by date, the Tool Catalog shows it set aside, and the set-aside lapses at the end of its collect-by date (Expire Hold).

Trigger & Actor

  • Pattern: automation. The Hold Fulfiller, a system processor, watches the Holds To Fulfill list (slices/holds-to-fulfill.md). No person fulfils holds; only the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold, and it is not exposed to neighbors or the shed manager.
  • Triggering condition: a tool is on the list: it is in the shed, not set aside for anyone, and at least one hold on it is waiting. Each item names the tool, the hold at the front of its queue, and that hold's holder.
  • When it acts: the list changes only when an event lands (a return, an expiry, a cancellation, a closure), so the Hold Fulfiller acts whenever the list changes, on each item that appears.
  • What it does: it issues Fulfill Hold for the item's hold. If the command is refused or is a repeat, nothing is recorded and the processor moves on; the list will show the tool again with its new front hold, if there is one.

Command / Input

Command: Fulfill Hold

A HoldId is a UUID. One clock reading is taken when the command is handled. "Today" (for collectByDate) is that moment's calendar date in the shed's local time zone, and the event's fulfilledAt is that same moment.

FieldTypeRequiredRules / Validation
holdIdHoldIdyesThe hold to fulfil: the front waiting hold of its tool (INV-FUL-2). Must be a hold that has been placed (INV-FUL-9).

Trigger

Triggered by: processor Hold Fulfiller, also in this slice, reading Holds To Fulfill.

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Hold Fulfilled → context Holds Read by: Holds To Fulfill (the tool leaves the list), Tool Catalog (set aside), My Holds (ready for pickup), Pickup Notices To Send (the holder's email), Pickups To Expire (the collect-by date to watch), and Undelivered Notices (a later pickup-email failure's details).

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
holdIdHoldIdyesFrom the command.
toolIdToolIdyesSet by the system: the tool on the hold's Hold Placed.
toolNameTextyesSet by the system: the tool's name on the hold's Hold Placed.
neighborIdNeighborIdyesSet by the system: the holder on the hold's Hold Placed.
neighborNameTextyesSet by the system: the holder's name on the hold's Hold Placed.
neighborEmailTextyesSet by the system: the holder's email current at fulfilment: Hold Placed.neighborEmail, replaced by any Neighbor Email Changed for the holder since.
collectByDateDateyesSet by the system: today plus 3 days. The set-aside lapses at the start of the day after it, shed local time.
fulfilledAtInstantyesSet by the system: the UTC moment the event is recorded.

collectByDate is recorded here once, so every reader uses the same date and none works it out.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. The Hold Fulfiller reads Holds To Fulfill, specified in slices/holds-to-fulfill.md. Hold Fulfilled takes the tool off that list and sets it aside in the Tool Catalog, My Holds and the pickup lists. All are eventually consistent: the list may still show a tool for a moment after it was fulfilled, which is why the command itself refuses a second fulfilment.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-FUL-2: A tool is set aside for the hold at the front of its queue: the hold, still waiting, whose Hold Placed was recorded first.
    • Queue order is the order the Hold Placed events were recorded, never a comparison of times.
  • INV-FUL-3: A hold is fulfilled only while the tool is in the shed and not set aside for anyone, and the hold is still waiting.
    • In the shed: no loan of the tool is open (Tool Checked Out without Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan), and it hasn't been retired.
    • Not set aside: no other hold on the tool has been fulfilled and not yet ended.
    • Still waiting: the hold hasn't been fulfilled and hasn't ended. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, the holder checks the tool out, the tool is retired or recorded lost, or the holder closes their account.
  • INV-FUL-4: A tool is set aside for one holder at a time.
    • A lapsed set-aside still counts until its Hold Expired is recorded. Only then is the next hold fulfilled.
  • INV-FUL-5: A fulfilled hold's collect-by date is the fulfilment date plus 3 days.
    • Until the end of that date, only the holder may check the tool out (Check Out Tool, INV-CHK-3). The holder collects it with an ordinary checkout.
  • INV-FUL-6: When a set-aside ends without the holder collecting it and another hold is waiting, the next hold is fulfilled in the same way.
    • A set-aside ends this way when the hold expires or is cancelled, or the holder closes their account. With no hold waiting, nothing is fulfilled and the tool becomes available.
  • INV-FUL-8: The front hold is fulfilled even if its holder can't collect right now, because they are suspended or have an overdue loan.
    • They keep their place. If they can't collect by the end of the collect-by date, the hold expires and the next hold is fulfilled.
  • INV-FUL-9: The hold must exist.
  • INV-FUL-10: Fulfilling a hold that is already fulfilled records nothing new.
    • A repeated request for that hold succeeds, so a list read twice never sets a tool aside twice or moves its collect-by date.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ben's hold H1 on the cordless drill was placed before Cara's hold H2. Today is 10 October in the shed's local time.

  • Happy path: tool returned with holds waiting (INV-FUL-2, INV-FUL-5)
    • Given: Ana returned the drill on 10 October. H1 and H2 are waiting, so the drill is on Holds To Fulfill with H1 at the front.
    • When: the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold for H1
    • Then: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1: the drill, Ben, collect by 13 October.
  • Next hold after an expired set-aside (INV-FUL-6)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben under H1, Hold Expired has been recorded for H1, and H2 is waiting
    • When: the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold for H2
    • Then: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H2: the drill, Cara, collect by 13 October.
  • Next hold after a cancelled set-aside (INV-FUL-6)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben under H1, Ben cancelled H1, and H2 is waiting
    • When: the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold for H2
    • Then: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H2.
  • Next hold after the holder closes their account (INV-FUL-6)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben under H1, Ben closed his account, and H2 is waiting
    • When: the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold for H2
    • Then: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H2.
  • Front holder is suspended (INV-FUL-8)
    • Given: the drill is back in the shed with H1 at the front, and Ben is suspended
    • When: the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold for H1
    • Then: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1: the drill, Ben, collect by 13 October.
  • Front holder has an overdue loan (INV-FUL-8)
    • Given: the drill is back in the shed with H1 at the front, and Ben has an overdue loan
    • When: the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold for H1
    • Then: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1.
  • The list is read twice (INV-FUL-10)
    • Given: Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for H1, and the list showed the drill once more before it caught up
    • When: the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold for H1 again
    • Then: the command succeeds and records nothing new. The collect-by date stays 13 October.
  • The holder collected first (INV-FUL-3)
    • Given: the drill came back with H1 at the front, and Ben checked it out before the Hold Fulfiller acted, which ended H1
    • When: the Hold Fulfiller issues Fulfill Hold for H1
    • Then: refused with hold-ended: "This hold has already ended." No event is recorded.
  • Not the front of the queue (INV-FUL-2)
    • Given: the drill is back in the shed with H1 and H2 waiting
    • When: a Fulfill Hold for H2 arrives
    • Then: refused with not-front-of-queue: "This hold isn't at the front of its tool's queue." No event is recorded.
  • Tool still set aside for someone else (INV-FUL-4)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben under H1, his collect-by date has passed, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded for H1 yet. H2 is waiting.
    • When: a Fulfill Hold for H2 arrives
    • Then: refused with tool-set-aside: "This tool is already set aside for a holder." No event is recorded. Once Hold Expired is recorded for H1, H2 can be fulfilled.
  • Tool on loan (INV-FUL-3)
    • Given: the drill is on loan to Ana, and H1 is waiting
    • When: a Fulfill Hold for H1 arrives
    • Then: refused with tool-checked-out: "This tool is already checked out." No event is recorded.
  • Hold cancelled before the fulfiller acted (INV-FUL-3)
    • Given: the drill came back with H1 at the front, and Ben cancelled H1 before the Hold Fulfiller acted
    • When: a Fulfill Hold for H1 arrives
    • Then: refused with hold-ended. No event is recorded. The list shows the drill with H2 at the front.
  • Unknown hold (INV-FUL-9)
    • Given: no hold H9 has been placed
    • When: a Fulfill Hold for H9 arrives
    • Then: refused with hold-not-found: "There is no such hold." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

A refusal records nothing; the Hold Fulfiller logs it with the hold ID and moves on. No person sees these reasons. The name is the contract; the sentence is the log text.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. hold-not-found (INV-FUL-9).
  2. If Hold Fulfilled is already recorded for the hold, the command succeeds and records nothing (INV-FUL-10).
  3. hold-ended (INV-FUL-3).
  4. tool-checked-out (INV-FUL-3).
  5. tool-set-aside (INV-FUL-4).
  6. not-front-of-queue (INV-FUL-2).
ReasonSentenceRule
hold-not-foundThere is no such hold.INV-FUL-9
hold-endedThis hold has already ended.INV-FUL-3
tool-checked-outThis tool is already checked out.INV-FUL-3
tool-set-asideThis tool is already set aside for a holder.INV-FUL-4
not-front-of-queueThis hold isn't at the front of its tool's queue.INV-FUL-2

hold-not-found, hold-ended and tool-checked-out mean the same conditions as in Cancel Hold and Check Out Tool. A retired tool's holds have all ended, so a retired tool shows as hold-ended. A missing or malformed hold ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: a repeated Fulfill Hold for a hold already fulfilled succeeds and records nothing (INV-FUL-10).

Requests at the same moment: Fulfill Hold is decided against the tool's holds and loans as already recorded, one at a time per tool, so at most one hold on a tool is set aside at once. A holder's checkout, a cancellation or an expiry landing at the same moment is decided in the same order: whichever is recorded first stands.

There are no external calls in this slice. The pickup email is sent by Send Pickup Notice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: Fulfill Hold is internal. Only the Hold Fulfiller issues it.
  • PII & compliance: Hold Fulfilled links a neighbor to a tool and a date. No name or email.
  • Performance / SLA: a tool is set aside within moments of the event that put it on the list. Nothing on record sets a tighter limit.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId. Queue order is the order these were recorded.
    • Hold Fulfilled (this slice): holdId, toolId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool), Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId, toolId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • The Hold Fulfiller reads Holds To Fulfill's items: toolId, holdId, neighborId (slices/holds-to-fulfill.md).
    • These keys match the deep-passed docs, and the Hold Fulfilled shape matches what undelivered-notices.md, check-out-tool.md and holds-to-fulfill.md read.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Holds To Fulfill, Tool Catalog, My Holds, Pickup Notices To Send, Pickups To Expire and Undelivered Notices. Check Out Tool reads collectByDate to enforce the holder's claim, and Expire Hold to find lapsed set-asides.

Open Questions

None.

State Viewv2DraftDelta pending

Slice: Pickups To Expire

Step 24 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · after Undelivered Notices — pickup notice failed · before Expire Hold · State View

Intent

The pickup expirer's to-do list: every tool currently set aside for a holder, with the date it must be collected by. The expirer works through the ones whose collect-by date has passed, so a set-aside the holder doesn't collect in time ends and the tool moves on to the next neighbor.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the Pickup Expirer, a system processor in the Expire Hold slice (slices/expire-hold.md). No person or screen reads this list.
  • What the expirer does with it: it reads the set-asides that are due to expire, and issues Expire Hold for each.

Read Model / View

  • View: Pickups To Expire built from events: "Hold Fulfilled", "Hold Collected", "Hold Cancelled", "Hold Expired"
  • Consumed by: the Pickup Expirer (Expire Hold). Internal: no ui.
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a set-aside joins or leaves shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Whether a set-aside is due to expire is worked out when the list is read, from collectByDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so it becomes due from the first read after the midnight that ends its collect-by date.

The view keeps one row for every live set-aside; the query returns only those due to expire. HoldId, ToolId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
holdIdHoldIdHold Fulfilled.holdId.
toolIdToolIdHold Fulfilled.toolId.
neighborIdNeighborIdHold Fulfilled.neighborId: the holder.
collectByDateDateHold Fulfilled.collectByDate, as recorded there. Never worked out here.
dueToExpireBoolDerived: yes when today's date in the shed's local time zone is after collectByDate (INV-PTE-2). Worked out when the list is read.

When a row leaves the view. A set-aside's row is removed when:

  • Hold Collected is recorded for its hold;
  • Hold Cancelled or Hold Expired is recorded for its hold (retiring the tool or closing the holder's account records Hold Cancelled for it).

Nothing puts a row back. A tool recorded lost is always on loan, so it is never set aside, and Tool Lost needs no rule here.

Queries

  • List set-asides to expire. Takes nothing. Returns every row whose dueToExpire is yes, with holdId, toolId, neighborId and collectByDate. There is no paging. The order doesn't matter to the expirer, which expires each one.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-PTE-1: A set-aside is on the list from Hold Fulfilled, with the collect-by date recorded on it.
    • One row per Hold Fulfilled; nothing else creates a row.
  • INV-PTE-2: A set-aside is due to expire once its collect-by date has passed.
    • This is worked out by comparing the collect-by date with today. No event marks the set-aside as lapsed.
    • The set-aside lapses at the start of the day after its collect-by date, in the shed's local time. On the collect-by date itself it is not due.
  • INV-PTE-3: When the holder checks the tool out, the set-aside leaves the list.
  • INV-PTE-4: When the holder cancels the hold, the set-aside leaves the list.
  • INV-PTE-5: When Hold Expired is recorded, the set-aside leaves the list.
  • INV-PTE-6: When the tool is retired or the holder closes their account, the set-aside leaves the list.
    • Both end the hold: Retire Tool and Close Account record Hold Cancelled for it, which this list hears like any cancellation.
  • INV-PTE-9: A checkout by anyone other than the holder doesn't take the set-aside off the list.
    • After the cut-off, the next holder, or anyone if no hold is waiting, may check the tool out before Hold Expired is recorded (Check Out Tool, INV-CHK-3b). The lapsed hold still gets its Hold Expired.
  • INV-PTE-10: Applying the same event twice leaves the list as if it had been applied once.

The pickup window runs regardless of whether the holder can collect: it doesn't pause while the holder is suspended or has an overdue loan (Fulfill Hold, INV-FUL-8; Expire Hold). This list treats every set-aside alike.

The list has no screen; only the Pickup Expirer reads it.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Hold Fulfilled was recorded for Ben's hold H1 on the cordless drill on 10 October, with a collect-by date of 13 October.

  • Tool set aside (INV-PTE-1)
    • Given: the list is empty
    • When: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1: the drill, Ben, collect by 13 October
    • Then: H1 is on the list, collect by 13 October, not due to expire.
  • On the collect-by date (INV-PTE-2)
    • Given: H1 is on the list, and Ben hasn't collected the drill
    • When: the list is read during 13 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 is not returned: it isn't due yet.
  • Collect-by date passes (INV-PTE-2)
    • Given: H1 is on the list, and Ben hasn't collected the drill
    • When: the list is read after the start of 14 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 is returned as due to expire. Nothing is recorded until the expirer acts.
  • Holder collects in time (INV-PTE-3)
    • Given: H1 is on the list
    • When: Hold Collected is recorded for H1 on 12 October
    • Then: H1 leaves the list.
  • Someone else takes a lapsed set-aside (INV-PTE-9)
    • Given: H1 is on the list and due to expire, and Cara's hold was waiting behind it
    • When: Cara checks the drill out on 14 October, so Hold Collected is recorded for her hold, not H1
    • Then: H1 stays on the list, still due to expire. It leaves only when Hold Expired is recorded for it.
  • Holder cancels (INV-PTE-4)
    • Given: H1 is on the list
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 leaves the list.
  • Set-aside expires (INV-PTE-5)
    • Given: H1 is on the list and due to expire
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 leaves the list. If Hold Fulfilled is then recorded for Cara's hold H2, H2 joins the list with its own collect-by date.
  • Tool retired (INV-PTE-6)
    • Given: H1 is on the list
    • When: Retire Tool records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Tool Retired for the drill
    • Then: H1 leaves the list.
  • Holder closes their account (INV-PTE-6)
    • Given: H1 is on the list
    • When: Close Account records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Neighbor Account Closed for Ben
    • Then: H1 leaves the list.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-PTE-10)
    • Given: H1 is on the list once
    • When: the same Hold Fulfilled for H1 is applied again
    • Then: H1 is still on the list once, with the same collect-by date.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-PTE-10). An event applied a second time leaves the list as it was after the first.
  • Events for a set-aside no longer listed: once a row has left, a later Hold Collected, Hold Cancelled or Hold Expired for it changes nothing.
  • The expirer reads a set-aside twice before Hold Expired lands: the list may return the same hold on two reads in a row. Expiring a hold once is Expire Hold's rule, enforced when it records Hold Expired; this list raises no errors of its own.
  • Daylight-saving changes: the day boundary is midnight in the shed's local time zone, whatever its offset from UTC that day.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: read only by the Pickup Expirer. No person or screen reads it.
  • PII & compliance: holds IDs and dates only. No names or emails.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above. How soon a due set-aside is expired is Expire Hold's concern.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId, collectByDate.
    • Hold Collected (Collect Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Cancelled is also recorded by Retire Tool and Close Account, one per hold they end.
    • These keys match the deep-passed docs and the Hold Fulfilled convention.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The Pickup Expirer reads it and issues Expire Hold.

Open Questions

None.
